result.title: Build.Tests on Windows: eight Linux-only ServiceUpdateTests cases run and fail (mkfifo, Unix file modes, directory symlinks)
result.summary: ServiceUpdateTests marks six Linux service-update methods (8 cases) with Trait Platform=Linux and Category=Integration, but nothing excludes or adapts them on Windows, and Build.Tests runs directly as the infrastructure check (never through Nuke Test, whose Category!=Integration filter would hide them). On Windows they fail: LinuxPreflight_RejectsSpecialApphostAndTextInputs (4 cases) and LinuxPreflight_RejectsSpecialStageFiles cannot start mkfifo; LinuxArchive_UsesPrivateMetadataPreservingCommands and LinuxPreflight_RejectsSymlinkRootAndNonexecutableStage(symlink: False) throw PlatformNotSupportedException for Unix file modes; LinuxReplacement_DoesNotFollowSymlinks fails with UnauthorizedAccessException (symlink creation). No skips are allowed by the operator, so the tests need per-OS behavior (as BUG-BASELINE-004 did for Windows-only tests). Pre-existing: Build.Tests never ran on Windows before (the retired CI ran only ./build.ps1 Test).
